The case / 02

Students often need answers scattered across university pages. We built a campus web-agent demo for University of Toronto and Waterloo questions, with cited sources attached to answers.

Question / example

A student asks about a course requirement. The system visits relevant pages, returns the answer with citations, and shows which sources were readable, skipped, or behind a login.

My contribution

I directed the team delivery and brought frontend, backend, and live browser workflows together. I worked on source routing, evidence extraction, and coverage reporting so the demo could surface inaccessible or insufficient sources.

What a student sees

The Course Desk presents the question and cited answer. A read-only browser view shows the pages being checked, while a coverage receipt distinguishes readable sources from login-walled or skipped ones. Prior questions can be reopened from browser-local history.

Behind that interface, a React frontend talks to a Fastify service. Steel and Playwright drive source visits; evidence extraction and shared contracts keep the browser result connected to the answer.

Decisions that mattered

  • Show evidence. A useful answer should point to the sources behind it, rather than ask the student to trust an opaque summary.
  • Report gaps. A source that cannot be reached or does not answer the question should be visible as a limitation.
  • Keep browser runs contained. Preflight and regression checks covered routing, execution, cancellation, cleanup, and evidence integration.

Outcome and scope

We delivered a repeatable hackathon demo. It demonstrates an approach to evidence-backed campus answers. Live research requires configured API access, and some private course pages still require login. Fixture demos are labeled separately from live browsing.

A cited answer can still omit a relevant rule, so missing or ambiguous evidence is reported rather than silently filled in. The diagram above is a system map, not a live product capture.
